pathway.title: Alta Equipment Group Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is adequate: exclusive OEM territories and a spread of customers support an aftermarket-heavy earnings stream, but equipment sales and rental income are cyclical and supplier-dependent. Parts and service were 29.83% of FY2025 revenue and 53.39% of gross profit after rental depreciation, no customer exceeds 1% of revenue, and Construction Equipment produced 60.83% of FY2025 revenue. In the first nine months of 2026 organic revenue fell 1.0% and Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.78%, with parts margins down 140 bp and service margins up 150 bp as management cut technician headcount and non-billable labor. Five OEMs supplied 49% of purchases and their finance arms renew floor plan lines each year, so the core is durable and the edge is exposed to supplier decisions. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 19, 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 37–39; calculation C8; calculation C9

Leverage is stretched and has risen since FY2023 while earnings fell. Total debt to calculated EBITDA rose from 3.47x at FY2023 to 4.50x at FY2025 and 4.65x for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and EBITDA cover of cash interest fell from 3.58x to 2.02x, because EBITDA fell 20.46% to USD 152.8 million and total debt rose 6.55% to USD 710.7 million. Counting floor plan payables of USD 325.7 million as debt lifts leverage to 6.78x, while the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA gives 4.38x; a committee should read 4.65x as the measure consistent with the issuer's debt definition and 6.78x as the conservative bound. At the last twelve months' pace of EBITDA less cash interest and capital expenditure, USD 48.7 million, repaying total debt would take 14.59 years, so deleveraging from cash flow is not a credible route to the 2029 maturity. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 18; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6

Free cash flow is not yet durable: the last twelve months turned positive on lower spending and the end of a floor plan paydown, not on earnings. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was an outflow of USD 16.2 million in FY2023, USD 13.5 million in FY2024 and USD 18.0 million in FY2025, then USD 64.2 million positive over the last twelve months. The USD 82.2 million swing is USD 59.1 million from manufacturer floor plan payables, which moved from a USD 55.4 million outflow in FY2025 to a USD 3.7 million net inflow, and USD 22.5 million from lower capital expenditure, leaving USD 0.6 million for everything else; operating cash flow before floor plan changes was USD 88.4 million in FY2025 and USD 89.0 million in the last twelve months. This sharpens Financial foundation, which stressed the nine-month floor plan inflow of USD 30.8 million: over twelve months the net floor plan change is small, and the gain is the end of FY2025's paydown, not new floor plan borrowing. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5

Liquidity is adequate until 2029 but cannot retire the 2029 debt, and how much of it is drawable is not established. Cash was USD 21.8 million and management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings under the ABL and floor plan facilities combined, up from USD 373.8 million at June 30, 2026 and USD 400.2 million at March 31, 2026 but below USD 424.4 million at FY2025. Printed limits less borrowings and letters of credit imply USD 530.9 million, USD 117.4 million more than reported, and the borrowing base is not printed, so reported availability is the figure to use. Cash plus reported availability covers 62.82% of the USD 692.9 million due in 2029. Management says cash flows, cash and borrowings will be adequate for the foreseeable future, and each one percentage point rise in variable rates would cut annual pre-tax earnings by USD 3.5 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55, 57; 10-Q_2026-06-30_altg_altg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-03-31_altg_altg-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C11

Refinancing capacity is the central uncertainty, because both main facilities fall due on 2029-06-01 with no equity cushion and no committed sponsor. The USD 192.9 million ABL and the USD 500.0 million second lien notes mature on the same day and are 95.59% of contractual principal including finance leases, so one refinancing, priced on 2028 earnings and market conditions, decides the credit. Equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million, the notes rank behind the ABL and the first lien floor plan facility, and no covenant level, borrowing base or lien capacity is printed, so the lender protections that would shape a refinancing are not established. The debt would normally become current from mid-2028, which is when a delayed refinancing would first show in reported liquidity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93; Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C10

Margins are stable but the mix inside them is shifting, and operating leverage is high. The consolidated gross margin was 26.9% for nine months 2026 against 26.8%, operating expenses were flat, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 9.33% in both periods, helped by service margins of 61.1% after technician headcount cuts. Parts margins fell to 33.1% from 34.5%, rental equipment sales margins fell 450 bp as aged fleet was sold, and healthcare costs rose. From FY2023 to FY2025 revenue fell 2.18% while calculated EBITDA fell 15.04%, so a small revenue miss moves earnings several times as much. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–40; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C9

Financial policy and governance risk is medium, and recent actions support creditors without committing to them. Distributions of USD 41.6 million over FY2023 to FY2025 exceeded the cash left after investment in every year, so they leaned on borrowing; since then the common dividend was halved and stopped, repurchases stopped and disposal proceeds of USD 25.9 million went to senior debt, but the preferred dividend of USD 2.2 million for nine months 2026 continues. Two officers hold an interest in OneH2, to which Alta paid USD 5.3 million for a hydrogen plant and which entered creditor assignment in June 2026. Ownership percentages, board detail and the terms of the 2026 investor agreements are not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41, 73–74, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 14, 24; calculation C10

runs.text: Aftermarket earnings carry more than half of gross profit, which cushions the cycle. Parts and service were 29.83% of FY2025 revenue but 53.39% of gross profit after rental depreciation, because service earns a margin of 59.45% against 14.07% on new and used equipment, so a fall in equipment sales removes less profit than revenue and supports debt service through a soft year. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9

Customers are spread and territories are exclusive, which limits revenue loss from any one buyer. No customer exceeds 1% of revenue and the top ten are about 6%, while Alta is the exclusive distributor of new equipment and replacement parts in substantially all territories, so losing a customer is immaterial to cash flow and parts demand follows the installed equipment base. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 13; Business & governance (CP-1A)

No principal falls due before 2029, which removes near-term refinancing pressure. The ABL and second lien notes both mature on 2029-06-01, and reported availability of USD 413.5 million gives room to fund seasonal working capital meanwhile, so a default before 2029 would need an operating shock large enough to break the borrowing base. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; calculation C7

Actions since mid-2025 are creditor-supportive. The common dividend was halved and stopped, repurchases stopped, capital expenditure fell 51.96% in nine months 2026, USD 25.9 million of disposal proceeds went to senior debt, and management cut rental fleet gross cost by USD 84.3 million, which lowers cash outflow and borrowing and shows that levers exist, although none is a stated policy. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41, 44, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 27; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10

Margins have held. The consolidated gross margin was 26.9% for nine months 2026 against 26.8%, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 9.33% in both periods, so cost actions have so far offset weaker volumes and keep cover from falling faster. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 38–39; calculation C8; calculation C9

The 2029 maturity is the main weakness. The USD 692.9 million of ABL and note principal falls due on one day against cash plus reported availability of USD 435.3 million, or 62.82%, so the credit depends on market access in 2028 and 2029 and on lenders accepting earnings that are lower than in FY2023. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; calculation C7

Leverage is high and cover is thin. Total debt is 4.65x EBITDA, 6.78x with floor plan payables, and EBITDA covers cash interest 2.02x, so a modest earnings fall cuts quickly into cash after interest and leaves little for debt reduction. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C6

Free cash flow depends on spending cuts and on floor plan timing. Free cash flow was negative in each of FY2023 to FY2025, and the positive last-twelve-month figure of USD 64.2 million is explained by lower capital expenditure and the end of a floor plan paydown, so it can reverse if spending or inventory financing normalizes. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation C5

Supplier dependence reaches liquidity. Five OEMs supplied 49% of purchases, suppliers may end distribution agreements or sell direct, and OEM finance arms renew floor plan lines annually after a credit review, so one supplier's decision could cut both product supply and working-capital funding. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 19, 30

Equity is a deficit and creditor protections are not visible. Stockholders' equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million, no sponsor is committed to support the equity, officers hold an interest in a related party that entered creditor assignment, and covenants, the borrowing base and board detail are not printed, so a stress case cannot assume outside support. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 14; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C10

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No new debt was issued in FY2025 or in the first nine months of 2026. The last issue was the USD 500.0 million senior secured second lien notes due 2029-06-01, completed on 2024-06-05 to refinance earlier second lien notes due April 2026, with a USD 6.7 million loss on extinguishment, to reduce variable-rate exposure and to provide liquidity and growth funding. On the same day the ABL facility was amended to raise its capacity to USD 520.0 million, including a USD 45.0 million Canadian sublimit, and to extend its maturity to 2029-06-01, and the ABL, floor plan and second lien agents signed an intercreditor agreement. The notes are guaranteed by each domestic subsidiary and secured by second-priority liens on substantially all assets, behind the first-priority liens that secure the ABL and the first lien floor plan facility. At September 30, 2026 USD 692.9 million of ABL and note principal falls due in 2029, and the floor plan and ABL facilities together are limited to USD 1,064.5 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93, 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; calculation C16

Other transactions are small. Alta bought the assets of a Quebec Yale dealer for USD 2.7 million on 2025-03-14 and sold three businesses with sale prices of USD 18.0 million (2025-05-01), USD 6.4 million (2025-08-29) and USD 1.5 million (2026-03-01), allocating each set of proceeds to reduce senior debt. The 2023 purchases of Burris, for USD 16.7 million in cash, and Ault, for USD 35.7 million including USD 5.3 million of Alta stock and a USD 3.2 million seller note, were the last large acquisitions, and net ABL borrowing of USD 91.3 million in FY2023 funded them together with working capital and rental fleet growth. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C13; calculation C15

No equity offering, sponsor funding or dividend recapitalization since 2023 is described in the filings. Alta raised its repurchase authorization twice, to USD 20.0 million in October 2024 and to USD 30.0 million in May 2025, and signed board observer and cooperation agreements with Mill Road Capital III on 2026-01-21, whose terms are not supplied. The June 2026 increase in the incentive plan share reserve dilutes equity holders but costs creditors no cash. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alta Equipment Group Inc. (issuer id altg-1759824), as of 2026-11-18, Full credit assessment (credit snapshot pathway). Scope: whether the five supplied SEC filings (annual reports for FY2024 and FY2025 and quarterly reports for Q1 to Q3 2026) can support the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit analyses, and what remains missing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five SEC filings are sufficient for a credit snapshot of Alta Equipment Group Inc. to September 30, 2026, giving creditors primary-source debt, liquidity and maturity evidence but no covenant-headroom or intercreditor test, because no credit agreement or indenture was supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three limits qualify that view. The filings state covenant compliance but print no covenant level, so headroom cannot be measured. Reported borrowing availability of USD 413.5 million is USD 117.4 million below what the printed facility limits imply, and the borrowing base is not printed. Board, ownership and compensation detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied. No source document is dated after the November 9, 2026 quarterly report, so the cutoff is respected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No executed governing document was supplied. The ABL credit agreement, the floor plan credit agreement and the indenture for the second lien notes due 2029 are described in the notes, and they and the intercreditor agreement are listed as exhibits incorporated by reference, but none is in the source set. No covenant level, definition, basket or springing test is printed in any of the five filings; each report states only that the company was in compliance with its financial covenants. No statement separates the issuer, the domestic subsidiary guarantors and the Canadian operations. Covenant headroom, lien priority, guarantor coverage and liability-management capacity therefore cannot be established from these sources. The executed documents named in the exhibit lists would close this gap. Severity: material.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Borrowing availability cannot be reconciled to the printed facility limits. At September 30, 2026 management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings under the ABL and floor plan facilities, while the printed combined limit of USD 1,064.5 million less USD 518.9 million outstanding and USD 14.7 million of letters of credit gives USD 530.9 million, a difference of USD 117.4 million. The filings print neither the borrowing base nor the collateral-based limits as amounts that would explain it, so both figures are carried with their roles and neither is chosen. Severity: material.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and ownership detail is incomplete. Directors, executive compensation, beneficial ownership and related-party transactions are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied. The Board Observer Agreement and the Cooperation Agreement with Mill Road Capital III, L.P. dated January 21, 2026 appear only in the exhibit list of the FY2025 annual report, with no terms printed. Severity: minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No market, rating, peer, portfolio or management-outlook input was supplied. The run settings declare no credit ratings, market quotes, peer set, deal terms or portfolio. None of the filings prints a credit rating level or numerical management guidance; the discussion of results offers qualitative outlook comments only. No current report on Form 8-K or earnings release is in the source set, so events between the November 9, 2026 quarterly report and the November 18, 2026 as-of date cannot be checked. Severity: minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The debt perimeter and earnings definitions must be carried by later analysis, not chosen here. Total debt and finance leases of USD 710.7 million exclude floor plan payables (USD 325.7 million carrying amount, presented as current liabilities) and operating lease liabilities (USD 116.0 million). Management's Adjusted EBITDA starts from net loss available to common stockholders, adds back preferred stock dividends and deducts floor plan interest on new equipment, and no covenant EBITDA definition is printed. Proceeds from rent-to-sell equipment sit in operating cash flow while transfers from inventory to the rental fleet are non-cash (USD 97.9 million in the nine months of 2026), so cash flow measures depend on that treatment. Severity: minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Period and version differences must be carried as well. Cash income taxes paid are printed for 2025 (by jurisdiction), 2024 and 2023 in the annual reports but not for the 2026 quarters, whose cash flow statements print cash paid for interest only. The latest debt maturity table is at December 31, 2025; the quarterly reports print maturity dates in text only. The FY2024 annual report corrected the FY2023 and FY2022 cash flow presentation by moving rent-to-rent proceeds of USD 5.4 million and USD 7.5 million from operating to investing cash flow, and the FY2025 annual report carries the corrected FY2023 figures. The FY2024 amounts compared across the two annual reports agree. Severity: minor.

Counting floor plan payables as debt lifts leverage to 6.78x. Equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million and no covenant level is printed, so headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage rose because earnings fell while debt grew. Reported EBITDA dropped from USD 192.1 million in FY2023 to USD 159.5 million in FY2024 and was USD 163.2 million in FY2025, while total debt grew from USD 667.0 million to USD 735.0 million, taking total debt to EBITDA from 3.47x to 4.50x. Rental revenues, which cost only USD 20.0 million before depreciation in FY2025, fell from USD 203.4 million to USD 179.8 million and rental equipment sales fell from USD 138.0 million to USD 109.1 million, so the fleet-funded earnings stream is shrinking and creditors hold a larger claim on a smaller earnings base.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–74; calculation C80; calculation C81; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest takes about half of EBITDA. Cash interest paid rose from USD 53.6 million in FY2023 to USD 76.4 million in FY2024 and USD 83.4 million in FY2025, so EBITDA cover fell from 3.58x to 1.96x. The last twelve months to September 30, 2026 lifted cover only to 2.02x, because cash interest eased to USD 75.6 million while EBITDA slipped to USD 152.8 million. At cover near 2x a modest earnings decline would cut quickly into the cash left after interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation C83; calculation C84; calculation C85; calculation C32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow after rental and other capital expenditure was an outflow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, of USD 16.2 million, USD 13.5 million and USD 18.0 million. The positive USD 64.2 million over the last twelve months rests on lower capital expenditure, USD 28.5 million against USD 51.0 million in FY2025, and on working capital rather than on higher earnings: nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 58.8 million includes a USD 30.8 million inflow from manufacturer floor plan payables, against an outflow of USD 28.3 million in nine months 2025. Floor plan payables are repaid as the financed equipment is sold, so part of the improvement is borrowed and can reverse.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; calculation C50; calculation C51; calculation C52; calculation C53

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate in the near term, but how much of it can fund debt service is not established. Cash is USD 21.8 million and management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings under the ABL and floor plan facilities combined, and the floor plan facilities primarily finance equipment inventory. The printed facility limits imply USD 530.9 million, USD 117.4 million more than reported, and the filings do not print the borrowing base. No principal falls due before June 2029, when USD 692.9 million of ABL and second lien note principal matures on one day, so a single refinancing decides the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 17–18, 55; calculation C58; calculation C59; calculation C60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage depends on the debt perimeter. Total debt of USD 710.7 million counts finance leases of USD 32.0 million but not floor plan payables of USD 325.7 million or operating lease liabilities of USD 116.0 million. With floor plan payables counted, total debt to EBITDA is 6.78x rather than 4.65x. The issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA deducts floor plan interest on new equipment as an operating cost, which is consistent with leaving floor plan payables out of debt, so a committee should read 4.65x as the issuer-consistent measure and 6.78x as the conservative bound.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 16–20, 35; calculation C55; calculation C67; calculation C86

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer deposits and deferred revenue, which fund operations without interest, were USD 33.4 million at September 30, 2026, down from USD 37.8 million at FY2023. The float is small against total debt of USD 710.7 million, so it neither supports liquidity materially nor hides a large claim; the obligation is to deliver equipment or service, and it is not a debt claim.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71; calculation C68; calculation C71

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The best case against a harsher view is the direction since June: leverage fell from 4.91x at June 30, 2026 to 4.65x, and net debt fell from USD 716.4 million at FY2025 to USD 688.9 million. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA, total debt is 4.38x and cover is 2.15x. No principal falls due before June 2029 and reported availability is USD 413.5 million. The view would improve if leverage keeps falling from 4.65x toward the 3.47x of FY2023 while cover moves above 2.02x, and it would weaken if reported availability fell below the USD 373.8 million of June 30, 2026 or the borrowing base proved smaller than the printed facility limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant levels, definitions and tests are not printed for any period from FY2023 to September 30, 2026. Every report states only that the company was in compliance with its financial covenants. This restricts covenant headroom, any covenant-based liquidity or default analysis and the debt stack's lender tests; no capacity is inferred. The action that would close it is the executed ABL credit agreement, floor plan credit agreement and indenture. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Borrowing availability cannot be reconciled to the printed facility limits at September 30, 2026. Management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings while the combined limit less borrowings and letters of credit gives USD 530.9 million, a difference of USD 117.4 million, and the borrowing base is not printed. This restricts the undrawn committed facilities in the liquidity chart and every liquidity measure built on it, which carry the reported figure. The action that would close it is the borrowing base certificate or the credit agreement definitions. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The individual floor plan facilities have no printed carrying value, margin, floor or maturity, and the legal rank of the OEM floor plan facilities and of the finance leases is not stated. These instruments therefore carry Not supplied cells in the instrument table and are left out of the debt stack. This restricts any secured-debt subtotal and the ranking of floor plan claims; the action that would close it is the floor plan credit agreements and the intercreditor agreement. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA, and the two differ by USD 1.2 million in FY2025 and USD 9.4 million over the last twelve months to September 30, 2026. This restricts every leverage and cover ratio to a labelled basis; the action that would close it is a covenant EBITDA definition, which no supplied document gives. Severity: Medium.

This restricts comparison with issuers that count floor plan debt; the action that would close it is a committee decision on the perimeter, with both measures stated. Severity: Medium.

This restricts the ladder to ABL and second lien note principal; the action that would close it is a maturity table in a later report. Severity: Medium.

This restricts cash-tax-based cash flow measures for 2026; the action that would close it is the cash flow supplemental disclosure in a later report. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Printed dashes are carried as Not supplied, not as zero, in these lines and periods: other income in Q3 2025; gain or loss on divestitures in FY2023, FY2024, Q1 2025 and Q3 2026; loss on debt extinguishment in FY2023 and FY2025; debt issuance cost and extinguishment lines in FY2023 and FY2025; acquisitions in FY2024, Q1 2026, H1 2026 and 9M 2026; divestiture proceeds in FY2023, FY2024 and Q1 2025; repurchases of common stock in FY2023, H1 2026 and 9M 2026; common dividends in the 2026 periods; and the foreign exchange effect in FY2023 and Q1 2025. Lines a period's statement does not print are likewise Not supplied. The totals tie without them, which indicates nil. This restricts nothing in the ratios; the action that would close it is the issuer's confirmation that a dash means nil. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Statements for FY2022, per-share data, share counts and the Q2 discrete quarter are not extracted, and segment assets and segment capital expenditures are not extracted. This restricts the history before FY2023 and the segment return measures; the action that would close it is extraction from the segment note and the FY2024 annual report. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating measures such as rental fleet utilization and backlog are described in words and not quantified, and the preferred stock's liquidation preference is not printed. This restricts operating trend analysis and the ranking of the preferred claim; the action that would close it is management disclosure of those measures. Severity: Low.

This restricts the post-balance-sheet adjustments to the sources read; the action that would close it is a current report review for that interval. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alta Equipment Group Inc. (issuer id altg-1759824), as of 2026-11-18, Full credit assessment (credit snapshot pathway). Scope: business model, ownership and control, governance, sponsor and shareholder behaviour, capital allocation and transaction history, drawn from the five supplied SEC filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alta is a diversified, OEM-anchored equipment dealer in which the supplied filings identify no controlling holder or sponsor, so creditors face operating and financial-policy risk more than extraction risk, and governance risk is medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Parts and service are 29.83% of FY2025 revenue but 53.39% of gross profit, and no customer exceeds 1% of revenue, which supports cash-flow durability. Against that, distributions of USD 41.6 million over FY2023 to FY2025 exceeded the cash left after investment in every year, so they leaned on borrowing, and preferred dividends continue with a stockholders' deficit of USD 47.1 million. The chief executive officer and chief financial officer hold an indirect minority interest in OneH2, which Alta paid USD 5.3 million to build a plant and which went into creditor assignment in June 2026; ownership, board and compensation detail is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 40, 71–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 14; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is durable at its core and dependent on suppliers at its edges. Parts and service were 29.83% of FY2025 revenue but 53.39% of gross profit after rental depreciation, while new and used equipment sales, 54.43% of revenue, earned a 14.07% margin. Alta is the exclusive distributor of new equipment and replacement parts in substantially all of its territories, no customer exceeds 1% of revenue and the top ten are about 6%, so cash flow is spread across many buyers. The dependency is on the manufacturers: five of them supplied 49% of equipment and parts bought in FY2025, a supplier may terminate a distribution agreement, and OEM finance arms provide floor plan lines that renew each year after a credit review, so one supplier's decision can reach both earnings and liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 13, 19, 30, 71–72; calculation C1; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings rest on Construction Equipment, and Material Handling is the weaker segment in 2026. Construction Equipment produced 60.83% of FY2025 revenue and 59.52% of segment Adjusted EBITDA before corporate costs, at a 9.04% margin. In the first nine months of 2026 Material Handling revenue fell 5.94% and its Adjusted EBITDA fell 5.01%, as new and used equipment sales dropped 11.67%, while Construction Equipment revenue rose 1.02% but its Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.74%. Reported group revenue fell 1.76%, but the issuer's organic revenue, which removes acquired and divested revenue, fell only 1.0%, to USD 1,302.5 million from USD 1,315.0 million, so nearly half of the reported decline comes from sold businesses. Group Adjusted EBITDA was USD 121.6 million against USD 123.8 million a year earlier, a margin of 9.33% in both periods, so the earnings base is flat to slightly lower and gives creditors no growth cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 105–107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 35; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The rental fleet is being shrunk on purpose, which turns fleet assets into cash at the cost of rental income. Management began a fleet optimization in mid-2024 aimed at excess rent-to-sell assets and weak-return classes, cutting rental fleet gross cost by USD 84.3 million from 2024-06-30 to 2025-12-31 and new equipment inventory by USD 51.5 million in FY2025. Rental revenue fell 11.60% in FY2025 and a further 4.38% in the first nine months of 2026, while rental equipment sales rose 18.42%, so part of the cash generated has come from selling fleet, not from earnings growth. Management describes rental rates as stable to slightly positive, but utilization is not quantified, so how far the fleet cuts have outrun demand is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; calculation C4; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling holder or sponsor is identified, which removes sponsor-extraction risk but leaves no named party committed to support the equity. Alta's shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange, ownership, board and compensation detail is incorporated from a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the market value of shares held by non-affiliates implies that affiliates held about 20% of the common shares in mid-2025. An investor, Mill Road Capital III, signed a board observer agreement and a cooperation agreement with Alta on 2026-01-21, but the filings give neither its holding nor the terms. Stockholders' equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million at September 30, 2026, so equity offers no loss-absorbing cushion, and no guarantee, cure right or equity injection by a holder is described in any of the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 111, 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5–6; calculation C10; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder distributions exceeded the cash left after investment in each of the last three years, so they leaned on borrowing; they have been cut back since, but not ended. Common dividends, preferred dividends and repurchases totalled USD 41.6 million over FY2023 to FY2025, 28.03% of operating cash flow, while operating cash flow less capital expenditure plus asset-sale proceeds was negative in two years and only USD 3.7 million in the third. The common dividend was halved in 2025 and none is printed for 2026, and repurchases of USD 5.8 million in FY2024 and USD 7.5 million in FY2025 have stopped, with USD 16.7 million of authorization still open. The preferred dividend continues, USD 2.2 million in the first nine months of 2026, despite the deficit. The filings give neither a reason for the changes nor a funding source, so the cut-back is observed, not committed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41, 73–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8, 58; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Corporate activity has shifted from buying to selling, which helps creditors modestly. Alta states that it completed 17 acquisitions since 2020 and describes its growth strategy as historically built on acquisitions, but cash spent on acquisitions was USD 45.6 million in FY2023 and USD 2.7 million in FY2025, with no acquisition cash printed for FY2024. The FY2023 purchases of Burris and Ault were funded, together with working capital and rental fleet growth, from net borrowing of USD 91.3 million under the ABL facility. Three disposals since May 2025 had sale prices of USD 18.0 million, USD 6.4 million and USD 1.5 million, USD 25.9 million in all, and each was allocated to reduce senior debt. The strategy has not been withdrawn, and pro forma earnings and integration results are not disclosed for any purchase, so a return to acquisitions would be a re-leveraging risk that the filings do not size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 74, 102–103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 30; calculation C13; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A related-party hydrogen investment is small but now unresolved. The chief executive officer and chief financial officer together hold an indirect, non-controlling minority interest in OneH2, to which Alta has paid USD 5.3 million to build and commercialize a hydrogen production plant for Alta. OneH2 assigned its assets for the benefit of its creditors on 2026-06-24 and the chief executive officer left its board. The total paid has not risen since the FY2024 report, which expected the plant to be operational in the first half of 2025; the FY2025 report moved that to the first half of 2026, and the 2026 reports give no start-up date. Management reports no indication of impairment and is considering commercialization opportunities, but the recoverable value of the plant and any further payments owed are not stated. Hydrogen fuel purchases from OneH2 were USD 0.6 million in FY2025, USD 1.6 million in FY2024 and USD 0.4 million in FY2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is adequate for monitoring, with one past correction and gaps in creditor-specific terms. The auditor's report on the FY2025 statements is dated 2026-02-26, management concluded that internal control over financial reporting was effective, and the FY2024 annual report corrected an error that had put rent-to-rent equipment sale proceeds in operating rather than investing cash flow, overstating operating cash flow by USD 7.5 million in FY2022 and USD 5.4 million in FY2023. The credit agreements, the indenture and the Series A preferred terms are not in the filings, so creditor protections must be taken from documents not supplied. Separately, 23.64% of employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements, two of which expire in 2027, and one multiemployer pension plan is in the red zone with a rehabilitation plan and a surcharge, a USD 1.7 million annual contribution whose withdrawal liability is not quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 68, 104–105, 108–109; calculation C9; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Alta presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is borrowing-funded distributions that are now curtailed, which matters because every dollar paid out while cash after investment was negative added to the claims that mature together in 2029 and implies a refinancing that depends on cash flow, not on outside support. Countervailing evidence is the stop to common dividends and repurchases, the use of disposal proceeds to repay senior debt and the cut to capital expenditure. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the terms of the 2026 investor agreements and the credit agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 74, 92–93, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8, 18, 24; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case that governance risk is higher than medium is a pattern of paying out cash the business had not generated: distributions of USD 41.6 million over three years, repurchases in loss years, a preferred dividend still paid with a stockholders' deficit of USD 47.1 million, and two senior officers holding an interest in a related party that has failed. The strongest case that it is lower is behaviour since mid-2025: common dividends and repurchases stopped, capital expenditure fell 51.96% in the first nine months of 2026, and USD 25.9 million of disposal proceeds went to senior debt. The view would worsen on evidence of a holder with control of the vote or a cooperation agreement that favours distributions or a sale, wide restricted-payment capacity in the credit agreements combined with resumed dividends or repurchases, or a further payment to OneH2. It would improve if the proxy statement shows an independent board with no controlling holder, the credit documents block distributions while debt is high, and further quarters pass with no payment beyond the preferred dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Without the proxy statement, who holds the common shares and whether any holder can steer distributions or a sale is not established, so the medium rating rests on the absence of a controlling holder in the filings, not on a confirmed share register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Without the terms of the January 2026 board observer and cooperation agreements, whether an outside investor has gained influence over capital allocation is not established; terms that commit Alta to a sale process or repurchases would raise the risk level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreements and indenture were not supplied, so capacity to pay dividends, make investments or add liens is unknown and willingness to distribute is read only from what Alta actually paid; the distribution findings carry no capacity test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The hydrogen plant's carrying value and any commitment to OneH2 are not stated, so whether USD 5.3 million is recoverable is not established and the related-party finding is sized only by amounts paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pro forma earnings and integration results for acquisitions, and the liquidation preference and redemption terms of the Series A preferred, are not printed, so acquisition discipline is judged from spending and funding alone and the preferred claim cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt was issued in FY2025 or in the first nine months of 2026. The last issue was the USD 500.0 million senior secured second lien notes due 2029-06-01, completed on 2024-06-05 to refinance earlier second lien notes due April 2026, with a USD 6.7 million loss on extinguishment, to reduce variable-rate exposure and to provide liquidity and growth funding. On the same day the ABL facility was amended to raise its capacity to USD 520.0 million, including a USD 45.0 million Canadian sublimit, and to extend its maturity to 2029-06-01, and the ABL, floor plan and second lien agents signed an intercreditor agreement. The notes are guaranteed by each domestic subsidiary and secured by second-priority liens on substantially all assets, behind the first-priority liens that secure the ABL and the first lien floor plan facility. At September 30, 2026 USD 692.9 million of ABL and note principal falls due in 2029, and the floor plan and ABL facilities together are limited to USD 1,064.5 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions are small. Alta bought the assets of a Quebec Yale dealer for USD 2.7 million on 2025-03-14 and sold three businesses with sale prices of USD 18.0 million (2025-05-01), USD 6.4 million (2025-08-29) and USD 1.5 million (2026-03-01), allocating each set of proceeds to reduce senior debt. The 2023 purchases of Burris, for USD 16.7 million in cash, and Ault, for USD 35.7 million including USD 5.3 million of Alta stock and a USD 3.2 million seller note, were the last large acquisitions, and net ABL borrowing of USD 91.3 million in FY2023 funded them together with working capital and rental fleet growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No equity offering, sponsor funding or dividend recapitalization since 2023 is described in the filings. Alta raised its repurchase authorization twice, to USD 20.0 million in October 2024 and to USD 30.0 million in May 2025, and signed board observer and cooperation agreements with Mill Road Capital III on 2026-01-21, whose terms are not supplied. The June 2026 increase in the incentive plan share reserve dilutes equity holders but costs creditors no cash.

This restricts the ownership register, the control conclusion and the governance risk level to the absence of a controlling holder in the filings; the action that would close it is the 2026 proxy statement. Severity: High.

This restricts any view on whether an outside investor can influence distributions, repurchases or a sale; the action that would close it is the current report filed on 2026-01-22 and its exhibits. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit agreements, indenture and intercreditor terms are not supplied, so restricted-payment, investment, lien and asset-transfer capacity cannot be assessed and no sponsor or shareholder willingness is inferred from capacity. This restricts the distribution flags to what Alta actually paid; the action that would close it is the executed documents with basket usage. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The funding source of dividends and repurchases and the way Alta meets the Delaware test for dividends while equity is negative are not stated. This restricts the finding that distributions leaned on borrowing to an inference from the cash flow statement; the action that would close it is management discussion in the next annual report. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The carrying value, operating status and commercialization plan of the hydrogen plant, and any commitments to OneH2, are not supplied, and the expected start-up date has slipped from the first half of 2025 to the first half of 2026 with no later date given. This restricts the size of the related-party exposure to amounts paid; the action that would close it is the notes to the next quarterly report. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rental fleet utilization and backlog are described in words and not quantified, and the OEM distribution and floor plan agreements are not supplied. This restricts the test of aftermarket and rental durability to reported revenue and gross profit by line, and the supplier-termination risk to the risk factor wording; the action that would close it is earnings materials and the dealer agreements. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pro forma earnings, integration cost and synergy results for acquisitions are not disclosed, and revenue by country is not printed. This restricts any view that acquisitions added earnings and the currency and regional exposure of the revenue base; the action that would close it is acquisition disclosures and a geographic revenue note. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The liquidation preference, redemption terms and dividend-blocking terms of the Series A preferred are not printed, and the multiemployer pension withdrawal liability is not quantified. This restricts the size and ranking of the preferred claim and of the pension contingent claim; the action that would close it is the certificate of designation and plan administrator estimates. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Events after the latest quarterly report, signed on 2026-11-09, cannot be checked from the supplied sources, and the latest report states no subsequent event. This restricts the events timeline to the sources read; the action that would close it is a current report review for the interval to the as-of date. Severity: Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alta Equipment Group Inc. (issuer id altg-1759824), as of 2026-11-18, Full credit assessment (credit snapshot pathway). Scope: the fundamental credit view built from the five supplied SEC filings and the three earlier module handoffs: business quality, leverage, free cash flow, liquidity, refinancing capacity, financial policy, downside path and monitoring.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alta is a stretched credit with a durable core: total debt is 4.65x EBITDA and EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.02x, so creditors depend on refinancing USD 692.9 million that falls due on one day in 2029, not on deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17–18; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Parts and service supply 53.39% of gross profit, no customer exceeds 1% of revenue and no principal falls due before 2029, but EBITDA has fallen 20.46% since FY2023 while total debt rose 6.55%, and the USD 64.2 million of last-twelve-month free cash flow comes from lower capital expenditure and a swing in floor plan payables, not from earnings. Cash plus reported availability of USD 435.3 million covers 62.82% of the 2029 principal, and stockholders' equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million with no sponsor to support it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8, 17–18, 55; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate: exclusive OEM territories and a spread of customers support an aftermarket-heavy earnings stream, but equipment sales and rental income are cyclical and supplier-dependent. Parts and service were 29.83% of FY2025 revenue and 53.39% of gross profit after rental depreciation, no customer exceeds 1% of revenue, and Construction Equipment produced 60.83% of FY2025 revenue. In the first nine months of 2026 organic revenue fell 1.0% and Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.78%, with parts margins down 140 bp and service margins up 150 bp as management cut technician headcount and non-billable labor. Five OEMs supplied 49% of purchases and their finance arms renew floor plan lines each year, so the core is durable and the edge is exposed to supplier decisions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 19, 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 37–39; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is stretched and has risen since FY2023 while earnings fell. Total debt to calculated EBITDA rose from 3.47x at FY2023 to 4.50x at FY2025 and 4.65x for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and EBITDA cover of cash interest fell from 3.58x to 2.02x, because EBITDA fell 20.46% to USD 152.8 million and total debt rose 6.55% to USD 710.7 million. Counting floor plan payables of USD 325.7 million as debt lifts leverage to 6.78x, while the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA gives 4.38x; a committee should read 4.65x as the measure consistent with the issuer's debt definition and 6.78x as the conservative bound. At the last twelve months' pace of EBITDA less cash interest and capital expenditure, USD 48.7 million, repaying total debt would take 14.59 years, so deleveraging from cash flow is not a credible route to the 2029 maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_altg_altg-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 18; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is not yet durable: the last twelve months turned positive on lower spending and the end of a floor plan paydown, not on earnings. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was an outflow of USD 16.2 million in FY2023, USD 13.5 million in FY2024 and USD 18.0 million in FY2025, then USD 64.2 million positive over the last twelve months. The USD 82.2 million swing is USD 59.1 million from manufacturer floor plan payables, which moved from a USD 55.4 million outflow in FY2025 to a USD 3.7 million net inflow, and USD 22.5 million from lower capital expenditure, leaving USD 0.6 million for everything else; operating cash flow before floor plan changes was USD 88.4 million in FY2025 and USD 89.0 million in the last twelve months. This sharpens Financial foundation, which stressed the nine-month floor plan inflow of USD 30.8 million: over twelve months the net floor plan change is small, and the gain is the end of FY2025's paydown, not new floor plan borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate until 2029 but cannot retire the 2029 debt, and how much of it is drawable is not established. Cash was USD 21.8 million and management reports USD 413.5 million of available borrowings under the ABL and floor plan facilities combined, up from USD 373.8 million at June 30, 2026 and USD 400.2 million at March 31, 2026 but below USD 424.4 million at FY2025. Printed limits less borrowings and letters of credit imply USD 530.9 million, USD 117.4 million more than reported, and the borrowing base is not printed, so reported availability is the figure to use. Cash plus reported availability covers 62.82% of the USD 692.9 million due in 2029. Management says cash flows, cash and borrowings will be adequate for the foreseeable future, and each one percentage point rise in variable rates would cut annual pre-tax earnings by USD 3.5 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55, 57; 10-Q_2026-06-30_altg_altg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-03-31_altg_altg-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing capacity is the central uncertainty, because both main facilities fall due on 2029-06-01 with no equity cushion and no committed sponsor. The USD 192.9 million ABL and the USD 500.0 million second lien notes mature on the same day and are 95.59% of contractual principal including finance leases, so one refinancing, priced on 2028 earnings and market conditions, decides the credit. Equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million, the notes rank behind the ABL and the first lien floor plan facility, and no covenant level, borrowing base or lien capacity is printed, so the lender protections that would shape a refinancing are not established. The debt would normally become current from mid-2028, which is when a delayed refinancing would first show in reported liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93; Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are stable but the mix inside them is shifting, and operating leverage is high. The consolidated gross margin was 26.9% for nine months 2026 against 26.8%, operating expenses were flat, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 9.33% in both periods, helped by service margins of 61.1% after technician headcount cuts. Parts margins fell to 33.1% from 34.5%, rental equipment sales margins fell 450 bp as aged fleet was sold, and healthcare costs rose. From FY2023 to FY2025 revenue fell 2.18% while calculated EBITDA fell 15.04%, so a small revenue miss moves earnings several times as much.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–40; 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance risk is medium, and recent actions support creditors without committing to them. Distributions of USD 41.6 million over FY2023 to FY2025 exceeded the cash left after investment in every year, so they leaned on borrowing; since then the common dividend was halved and stopped, repurchases stopped and disposal proceeds of USD 25.9 million went to senior debt, but the preferred dividend of USD 2.2 million for nine months 2026 continues. Two officers hold an interest in OneH2, to which Alta paid USD 5.3 million for a hydrogen plant and which entered creditor assignment in June 2026. Ownership percentages, board detail and the terms of the 2026 investor agreements are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41, 73–74, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 14, 24; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is the direction since June 2026: total debt to EBITDA fell from 4.91x to 4.65x, reported availability rose from USD 373.8 million to USD 413.5 million, cover improved from 1.96x at FY2025 to 2.02x, organic revenue fell only 1.0%, and management has cut capital expenditure, stopped dividends and repurchases and sold fleet. No principal is due until 2029, which leaves time to repair earnings. The strongest case for a worse view is that EBITDA has not recovered, the free cash flow gain is not earnings-driven, drawable availability may be smaller than printed limits because the borrowing base is unknown, and cash plus availability covers only 62.82% of the 2029 principal. The view would improve if leverage keeps falling toward the 3.47x of FY2023 with cover above 2.02x and operating cash flow before floor plan changes rises above the USD 89.0 million of the last twelve months. It would worsen if reported availability fell below USD 373.8 million, leverage rose above 4.91x, cover fell below 1.96x, or the borrowing base proved smaller than the printed limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; 10-Q_2026-06-30_altg_altg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 55; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer or sector benchmark was supplied, so whether leverage of 4.65x and cover of 2.02x are typical for equipment dealers and rental companies is not established, and the stretched verdict rests on the trend and on absolute cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside scenario applies an observed FY2023 to FY2025 earnings decline to the last twelve months, not a forecast, so the conclusion that liquidity is sufficient before 2029 holds for that scenario only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The choice of debt perimeter moves leverage between 4.65x and 6.78x, so the stretched verdict holds on either basis, but any comparison, covenant test or rating-style ratio must state which perimeter it uses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The repayment-time estimate uses EBITDA less cash interest and capital expenditure and leaves out cash taxes and working capital, so it indicates scale, not a forecast of debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management commentary on 2026 and later markets is dated to the latest filings, so the outlook could be wrong if demand moved after 2026-11-09.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Aftermarket earnings carry more than half of gross profit, which cushions the cycle. Parts and service were 29.83% of FY2025 revenue but 53.39% of gross profit after rental depreciation, because service earns a margin of 59.45% against 14.07% on new and used equipment, so a fall in equipment sales removes less profit than revenue and supports debt service through a soft year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customers are spread and territories are exclusive, which limits revenue loss from any one buyer. No customer exceeds 1% of revenue and the top ten are about 6%, while Alta is the exclusive distributor of new equipment and replacement parts in substantially all territories, so losing a customer is immaterial to cash flow and parts demand follows the installed equipment base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No principal falls due before 2029, which removes near-term refinancing pressure. The ABL and second lien notes both mature on 2029-06-01, and reported availability of USD 413.5 million gives room to fund seasonal working capital meanwhile, so a default before 2029 would need an operating shock large enough to break the borrowing base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Actions since mid-2025 are creditor-supportive. The common dividend was halved and stopped, repurchases stopped, capital expenditure fell 51.96% in nine months 2026, USD 25.9 million of disposal proceeds went to senior debt, and management cut rental fleet gross cost by USD 84.3 million, which lowers cash outflow and borrowing and shows that levers exist, although none is a stated policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41, 44, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 27; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have held. The consolidated gross margin was 26.9% for nine months 2026 against 26.8%, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 9.33% in both periods, so cost actions have so far offset weaker volumes and keep cover from falling faster.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 38–39; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2029 maturity is the main weakness. The USD 692.9 million of ABL and note principal falls due on one day against cash plus reported availability of USD 435.3 million, or 62.82%, so the credit depends on market access in 2028 and 2029 and on lenders accepting earnings that are lower than in FY2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high and cover is thin. Total debt is 4.65x EBITDA, 6.78x with floor plan payables, and EBITDA covers cash interest 2.02x, so a modest earnings fall cuts quickly into cash after interest and leaves little for debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow depends on spending cuts and on floor plan timing. Free cash flow was negative in each of FY2023 to FY2025, and the positive last-twelve-month figure of USD 64.2 million is explained by lower capital expenditure and the end of a floor plan paydown, so it can reverse if spending or inventory financing normalizes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier dependence reaches liquidity. Five OEMs supplied 49% of purchases, suppliers may end distribution agreements or sell direct, and OEM finance arms renew floor plan lines annually after a credit review, so one supplier's decision could cut both product supply and working-capital funding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity is a deficit and creditor protections are not visible. Stockholders' equity is a deficit of USD 47.1 million, no sponsor is committed to support the equity, officers hold an interest in a related party that entered creditor assignment, and covenants, the borrowing base and board detail are not printed, so a stress case cannot assume outside support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 14; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is the force that matters most to creditors, and buyer power matters least. Five OEMs supplied 49% of purchases, suppliers may appoint other distributors, sell direct or end agreements, and their finance arms renew floor plan lines each year, so supplier decisions reach earnings and liquidity. Buyers are fragmented, with no customer above 1% of revenue, and new entrants face OEM exclusivity and a shortage of skilled technicians, so rivalry and substitution are the pressures that show in margins: OEMs discount to win share, which is visible in the 14.07% margin on new and used equipment, and falling rental utilization makes renting a weaker offer for Alta's own fleet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic and political factors change the credit view, and social and technological factors do not on the evidence supplied. Variable-rate debt makes earnings sensitive to interest rates, tariff volatility and elevated channel inventories pressured equipment pricing in 2025, and public infrastructure funding supported construction demand, so these factors act through margins and the cost of the 2029 refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are limited. The lift truck industry expects bookings to strengthen in the second half of 2026, the annual report cites signs of stabilization in construction late in 2025 and management says Material Handling bookings improved with healthy backlog, and territory in-fill acquisitions could add parts and service, though acquisitions would add debt. Threats are tariff and rate volatility, supplier termination or non-renewal of floor plan lines, parts availability constraints in Material Handling and a refinancing window that opens in 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months earnings look flat to slightly lower, with cost actions offsetting soft volumes, and no maturity falls due. Interest expense was USD 7.7 million lower in nine months 2026 on smaller inventories and fleet and lower benchmark rates, operating expenses were flat, and management has reduced headcount, which supports margins; organic equipment sales are still falling and rental revenue falls as the fleet shrinks, so growth in cash flow would have to come from fleet and inventory release, which is finite.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the outlook is set by the 2029 refinancing: if EBITDA recovers toward the FY2023 level the debt can be refinanced at a leverage nearer 3.47x, and if it stays near USD 152.8 million the refinancing meets 4.65x leverage and cover near 2x with no equity cushion. Sector headwinds are tariff volatility, high channel inventories and rate sensitivity; tailwinds are infrastructure funding and an expected recovery in lift truck bookings, and none is quantified in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside path runs from equipment demand to earnings and then to the 2029 refinancing, and not to near-term liquidity. Softer construction and lift truck demand would cut equipment deliveries and rental utilization, shrink the inventory and receivables that support ABL advances and compress margins; if calculated EBITDA repeated its FY2023 to FY2025 fall of 15.04% from the last-twelve-month level it would be USD 129.8 million, cash interest cover would be 1.72x and total debt to EBITDA 5.48x, or 7.98x counting floor plan payables. The scenario is an assumption, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 55; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management levers are real but largely used. Capital expenditure is already only USD 28.5 million over twelve months, dividends and repurchases are stopped, and fleet sales and inventory release can raise cash, but they also reduce earning assets; EBITDA less cash interest and capital expenditure would fall to USD 25.7 million. Liquidity appears sufficient to avoid distress before 2029, because no principal falls due and USD 435.3 million of cash plus reported availability remains, but it would not protect an orderly refinancing of USD 692.9 million at that leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Alta presents an adequate business profile supported by aftermarket-heavy earnings, spread customers and exclusive OEM territories, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 4.65x, cover of 2.02x, a deficit in equity and a single maturity of USD 692.9 million in 2029. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was negative for three years and the recent gain comes from spending cuts and floor plan timing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA stabilizing near the current level, on the borrowing base holding and on supplier floor plan lines being renewed. The primary downside path is softer equipment demand that cuts earnings and collateral before the 2029 refinancing. Further analysis would require the credit agreements, the borrowing base, covenant levels, peer comparison and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: the single 2029 maturity of the ABL and second lien notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module Status: Ready with Limitations. No external source was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ABL borrowing base, covenant levels and any springing tests are not printed, so reported available borrowings of USD 413.5 million cannot be tested against the amount actually drawable, and the limits imply USD 117.4 million more. This restricts the liquidity conclusion to the reported figure and every stress statement about covenant headroom; the action that would close it is the ABL and floor plan credit agreements with compliance certificates. Severity: High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18, 55; Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The debt perimeter and the EBITDA definition move the ratios: total debt to EBITDA is 4.65x on carrying-value debt and calculated EBITDA, 6.78x with floor plan payables and 4.38x on Adjusted EBITDA. This restricts any peer, covenant or rating-style comparison to a stated basis; the action that would close it is a covenant EBITDA definition and a committee choice of perimeter. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 35; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No peer or sector benchmark and no agency or market view was supplied, so the business profile cannot be compared with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector and no rating-style view is assigned. This restricts the adequate profile label to absolute evidence; the action that would close it is a peer set with the same perimeter. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rental fleet utilization, backlog and quantified management guidance for 2027 and later are not supplied, and the filings describe market conditions in words. This restricts the outlook and the downside scenario to the observed FY2023 to FY2025 earnings sensitivity; the action that would close it is earnings materials with utilization, bookings and backlog. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_altg_altg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_altg_altg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership percentages, board composition, the credit agreements and the terms of the 2026 investor agreements are not supplied, so the financial policy conclusion rests on what Alta paid, not on what it may do. This restricts the medium governance risk level to the filings; the action that would close it is the proxy statement and the executed credit documents. Severity: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Events after the latest quarterly report, signed on 2026-11-09, cannot be checked from the supplied sources, and the post-balance-sheet adjustments in Financial foundation found none in the sources read. This restricts the liquidity and leverage figures to September 30, 2026; the action that would close it is a current report review to the as-of date. Severity: Low.
